newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Fernz forecasts strong profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Fernz forecasts strong profit growth.

text.p: New Zealand's Fernz Corp Ltd said on Thursday that after three months of trading in the current year, the tax-paid profit forecast of NZ$47.3 million was achievable. This would be a nine percent rise on the 1996 after-tax profit of $43.5 million.

Kerry Hoggard, Managing Director of the herbicide, fertiliser and drug manufacturer, told the annual meeting that although trading was marginally below budget in the first quarter, the company saw no reason to change its end-of-year profit forecast.
Hoggard said the company was forecasting after-tax profit to grow to NZ$58.7 million in the 1998 financial year and $70.3 million in 1999.

"The most significant growth is expected to come from the company's agchem and animal health business. Internationally, the company's agchem operations are ahead of budget while its chemical business is trading in line with forecast," he said.
Two deliveries of low-dose oral Interferon tablets have been made to China under a new registration received in July.
However, agricultural activities in New Zealand in the first three months, especially in fertiliser sales, were significantly below forecast following a very wet winter.
The newly-formed chemicals group will nearly double its contribution to profit in the next two years, while the oral Interferon project is forecast to be profitable by financial 1998.
In financial 1999, it is expected to contribute some NZ$5 million to after-tax profit.

Hoggard said a significant change was taking place in the regions of the world where the company was generating sales and that in the current financial year Oceania would account for less than half of sales (49 percent), North America 25 percent, Europe 18 percent and Asia eight percent.
Sales, which in the current year will reach $800 million, are forecast to hit $1 billion by 2000.
Hoggard said that strategically and in terms of international development, the company was in its "best ever position".
Fernz reported a net profit after tax of NZ$43.54 million in the year to May 31, which was up from $40.47 million a year earlier.

It recently bought the Australian, New Zealand and Singapore operations of the British chemical company Laporte plc for NZ$57 million and the crop and chemicals business of Holland's Akzo Nobel for $20 million.
